title: cdktn-bench published result row
description: One row of the published cdktn-bench results table: one trial's outcome, with everything needed to know whether it can be pooled with another row. REQUIRED fields are schema-required, not optional-by-convention — this is the direct fix for the chant-bench gap documented in docs/chant-bench-diff.md §5, where `run.substrate` was specified in that project's own plan but silently absent from all 122 published result JSONs because nothing enforced it. `equipping_hash` (gates/equipping.py) additionally guards against pooling results produced under a silently-different instruction, skill/MCP/plugin config, or Docker image.

schema_version.description: Version of this result-row schema. Bump on any breaking change to required fields; keep old rows valid against their own recorded schema_version rather than migrating them in place. 1.1 adds the REQUIRED `scenario_form` (ROADMAP.md §6b item 4), so a 1.0 row does not validate as 1.1.

scenario_form.description: REQUIRED. Which SCENARIO FORM this trial's task has -- the coarsest pooling boundary in the benchmark, applied by metrics/tokens_to_green.py BEFORE the train/holdout split and before the (arm, model, harness) cell. Rows of different forms are NEVER pooled into one headline number, at any n, in any estimator. The label is COMPOSITE: a step-shape base (greenfield | multi-step | pre-configured-account) plus a '-brownfield' suffix when the workspace is seeded, so the two independent dimensions can never collapse into one another ('brownfield' is the seeded greenfield base). Derived from the task directory alone by gates/emit_result.py::derive_scenario_form -- never guessed from a spec id -- and a row whose form could not be derived is never emitted: to_result_row refuses it the way it refuses a missing equipping_hash, rather than defaulting to 'greenfield'. The derivation, the base ordering and its justification, and the no-pooling rule are pre-registered in DECISIONS.md Amendment 36 (which rests on Amendment 26 §4, Amendment 27 §2 and Amendment 28 §6).

equipping_hash.description: sha256 hex digest from gates.equipping.compute_equipping_hash() over instruction.md, sorted skill/MCP/plugin config files, the resolved Docker image digest, and extra_cfg (model, harness flags). Two rows are only comparable if this matches.

oracle_version.description: Identifies exactly which oracle tier stack (structural asserts, Rego rules, and any hand-authored live check, docs/iac-abstraction-aws-bench-plan.md Phase 2) graded this trial, e.g. a git rev or oracle package version. Required so a later oracle fix never gets silently pooled with results graded under the old rules.

arm.description: Which arm produced this trial. awscdk and hcl-raw are the two primary arms, terraconstructs and hcl-modules are gated per spec (DECISIONS.md Amendments 2 and 46). hcl-modules rows cannot exist until that arm's image lands, so a reader that sees one is reading post-M3 data; the split is per scenario, so cell assignments carry over unchanged.

split_group.description: REQUIRED. The trial's scenario's train/holdout split group (generator/split.py::spec_group, specs/split.yaml, prereg §7.1 / DECISIONS.md Amendment 10), as of the time this row was emitted. "unclassified" means the scenario had no entry in specs/split.yaml yet (a scenario authored before the next re-split). Fixes the finding that the train/holdout split was unenforceable at the layer that matters -- the published number: metrics/tokens_to_green.py used to pool every row into cells keyed on (arm, model, harness) only, silently mixing train scenarios (the ones equipping is explicitly allowed to be tuned against) with holdout scenarios in one headline metric. Downstream analysis MUST stratify on this field for any headline number -- prereg §7.1 calls the train/holdout boundary "the methodological safeguard most likely to be skipped and most damaging if it is."

model.description: Bare Anthropic-API model name passed to the agent harness, e.g. "claude-sonnet-5" or "claude-haiku-4-5-20251001" (not a Bedrock ARN/us.anthropic.* id).

harness.description: The empty-vs-tuned equipping axis (prereg §2.2 / build plan Phase 2 item 4): "empty" = bare container, loop only; "tuned" = arm-specific MCP servers + skills injected.

validity_class.description: Output of Gates 2+3 of the three-gate integrity pattern (gates/README.md; values match gates/emit_result.py's VALID/INVALID_BYPASS/INVALID_INFRA exactly, so a gate-emitted record's validity_class always validates as-is). "valid" = the audit gate (gates/audit.py) found toolchain evidence in the trial's trajectory and no infra-failure signal was detected. "invalid-bypass" = the trial completed but never invoked the arm's own toolchain (e.g. answered via jq/cat instead of tsc/cdk synth/terraform validate) — not a scored failure of the arm, the trial never really tested it. "invalid-infra" = an infrastructure failure unrelated to code correctness (OOM, Docker-daemon unreachable, missing/invalid model-auth env var, the trial couldn't even be audited, or the audit gate found the toolchain was invoked but never actually available — command-not-found/SIGKILLed) — takes priority over a bypass verdict. validity_class is orthogonal to reward: an invalid row must never be pooled into a scored headline number, and reward/tokens are only meaningful when validity_class == "valid" — read validity_class first. NOTE: Gate 1 (preflight, gates/preflight.py) is intentionally NOT represented here. It is a pre-job check — "does this arm's toolchain even work in its container, offline" — that gates whether an arm's trials should run AT ALL, before any task/trial/equipping context exists to attach a schema row to; a preflight failure blocks a whole arm's job rather than producing a per-trial row. Run it with `make gate-preflight` (mk/rails.mk); its JSON report is not a validity_class value and is never expected to appear in a published result row.

tokens_input.description: Total prompt/input tokens for the trial (TrialResult.compute_token_cost_totals(), docs/aws-bench-guide.md §6).

tokens_output.description: Total completion/output tokens for the trial.

tokens_total.description: tokens_input + tokens_output (+ any cached tokens counted by the harness). Carried as its own field rather than always recomputed so a result row is self-describing without re-deriving it.

reward.description: Reward float written by the verifier (docs/aws-bench-guide.md §3: 1.0 = pass, 0.0 = fail; partial credit permitted where a task's verifier defines it). Meaningless when validity_class != "valid" — read validity_class first.

censored.description: True if the trial hit the budget cap (MAX_ITERS/MAX_TOKENS) before reaching a natural stop — right-censored for the tokens-to-green metric (build plan Phase 2 item 2), recorded rather than dropped. Independent of validity_class and reward.

tier1_not_verifiable.description: REQUIRED, default-false semantics: true iff gates/emit_result.py found a `/logs/verifier/tier1-not-verifiable` marker for this trial (the generated verifier, tests/tiers.py, tees it whenever the scenario's tier-1 policy.rego defines a `not_verifiable` rule, specs/SCHEMA.md §4.2.1, that fired against this trial's plan). Fixes a per-arm scoring bias (residual finding, 2026-08-06): a tier-1 value-content check (e.g. an IAM action allowlist) can go plan-time-unknown on the TF arms whenever a correct solution references another resource's provider-computed output — an entirely normal, idiomatic pattern — silently skipping that check while the CFN/awscdk arm (always fully static, no plan concept) has no such gap. Without this field, an identical wildcard-IAM violation scores 0.0 on awscdk but 1.0 on hcl_raw/terraconstructs with nothing in the row to show the tier-1 check was never actually evaluated for those two. Independent of validity_class and reward — always false when no marker was written (including for non-"valid" trials, which never run a verifier at all). Downstream analysis MUST flag or segment true rows separately: a reward of 1.0 with tier1_not_verifiable=true is not the same claim of correctness as reward 1.0 with tier1_not_verifiable=false, and pooling them silently reintroduces the exact bias this field exists to surface.

tier1_not_verifiable_detail.description: Free-text detail from the `/logs/verifier/tier1-not-verifiable` marker file itself (the human-readable message a scenario's `not_verifiable` Rego rule produced), present only when tier1_not_verifiable is true. Optional even then — informational only, never schema-enforced.

scenario.description: Scenario id (scenarios/<id>/scenario.toml [scenario].name) -- the aws-bench scenario SHARD ("anchor", or "anchor-k" -- generator/shards.py), each shared by many benchmark scenarios, so it must never be used to group/attribute results by benchmark scenario (sfn-jsonata vs. apigw-openapi, ...); use spec_id for that.

spec_id.description: REQUIRED-in-spirit (not schema-required, to keep old rows valid): the cdktn-bench BENCHMARK spec id (specs/<spec_id>.yaml, e.g. "apigw-openapi", "sfn-jsonata") this trial's task was generated from -- generator/gen.py::task_dir()'s own `<spec-id>-<arm>` naming convention. Distinct from `scenario` (the aws-bench scenario shard, "anchor" or "anchor-k", which many benchmark scenarios share) and from `task` (task.toml's own id). This is the field downstream per-scenario grouping (metrics/tokens_to_green.py::build_tier_attribution, _group_by_scenario/by_scenario/scenario_coverage) and prereg §7's paired-by-scenario analysis MUST key on -- `scenario` names a shard many benchmark scenarios share, so it collapses them into a few degenerate groups and cannot support that decomposition. Populated by gates/emit_result.py::to_result_row from its own `spec_id=` kwarg (already resolved there for split_group).

trial_id.description: Harbor trial name; joins this row back to <job_dir>/<trial_id>/{result.json,agent/trajectory.json}.

job_id.description: aws-bench job/run directory name this trial belongs to.

tokens_cached.description: Cached-read tokens, if the harness reports them separately from tokens_input.

cost_usd.description: Total cost in USD for the trial, if available (TrialResult.compute_token_cost_totals()).

n_llm_calls.description: Iteration count (LLM calls in the trial), for iterations-to-green. Populated by gates/emit_result.py::extract_n_llm_calls() from agent/trajectory.json (mirrors aws_bench/metrics/run_data.py::_llm_usage_from_trajectory's own n_llm_calls accumulation), since result.json's agent_result never carries this field itself. Falls back to the stream transcript's own num_turns when the step has no trajectory -- see audit_source.

audit_source.description: OPTIONAL provenance. Which file gate 2 (gates/audit.py) read the agent's tool calls from. ABSENT (equivalently "trajectory") on every row audited from harbor's ATIF agent/trajectory.json, which is the normal case. "claude-code-stream" means at least one step had no trajectory because harbor's own Claude Code converter rejected its output on a step-id gap (docs/upstream/harbor-trajectory-step-id-gap.md) and the audit read agent/claude-code.txt instead: same tool calls, same observation text, same degraded/bypass classification, but recorded so a reader can tell which rows exist only because of that fallback.

tokens_source.description: OPTIONAL provenance, set only when the token fields were recovered from the stream transcript's terminal result event because harbor's own agent_result carried nulls -- the same converter failure audit_source records. Absent means harbor priced the trial itself.

tier_evidence.description: Per-catch tier-attribution evidence (docs/iac-abstraction-aws-bench-plan.md Phase 2 item 3 / prereg §4's per-tier catch attribution), read by gates/emit_result.py::read_tier_evidence() from verifier/test-stdout.txt. tier0 is REAL per-assert evidence (each tier-"0" structural_assert echoes its own PASS/FAIL independently); tier1_status is a single BUNDLED verdict covering every tier-"1" structural_assert for this arm/scenario at once (the oracle itself only ever computes one opa-eval verdict per bundle -- there is no per-tier-1-catch breakdown to read). Absent entirely when verifier/test-stdout.txt doesn't exist (verifier never ran a static_tiers.sh-shaped test.sh); present with tier0={} and tier1_status=null when the file exists but a toolchain step failed before tier-0/1 ever ran.

tier0.description: structural_assert name -> "PASS" | "FAIL", for every tier-"0" assert this arm/scenario declares and that actually ran before any earlier toolchain step failed.

tier1_status.description: The single bundled tier-1 verdict the generated verifier (tests/tiers.py::tier_1) prints on its summary line, or null if the verifier never reached the tier-1 block (an earlier toolchain/tier-0 step already wrote reward.txt and exited). ENGINE_ERROR is the oracle's own failure -- an opa eval that aborted, or an oracle.hcl_traversal pre-parse that did not complete -- and gates to 0.0 on the specs that can emit it.

wall_seconds.description: Wall-clock duration of the trial in seconds.

validity_reason.description: Free-text detail for a non-"valid" validity_class (e.g. which preflight check failed, or the OOM/timeout signal observed) — required in spirit whenever validity_class != "valid", not schema-enforced since the exact detail is gate-specific.

blast_radius.description: OPTIONAL profile column (ROADMAP §2 "a profile, not a scalar", M1): how much infrastructure this solution's change actually moves. Computed by gates/blast_radius.py from the artifact the verifier persisted into /logs/artifacts and harbor collected into <trial>/artifacts/ -- never from a post-hoc re-run. The Terraform read is `resource_changes[]`, NOT `planned_values`: that array is flat, carries `module_address` and instance-keyed addresses, and holds the `change.actions` the counts are keyed on; `planned_values` is a desired-state tree with no actions in it, so it cannot express what gets replaced. ABSENT on a row whose trial persisted no usable artifact -- `blast_radius_unavailable` then carries the reason, and the two fields are mutually exclusive. Multi-step rows describe the FINAL step's artifact, the change the reward is attributed to.

source.description: Which document the counts were read from, because the three do not carry the same information. `terraform-plan` (`terraform show -json`) fills every bucket and both halves of the root/module split. `cloudformation-changeset` (DescribeChangeSet, `Changes[].ResourceChange` Action + Replacement) fills the buckets but has no module concept. `cloudformation-template` is what an awscdk trial carries with no deployment behind it -- a synthesized template states what will exist, not what a deployment would do to what is already there -- so `total` is its `Resources` count and `counts`/`root`/`module` are all null. A row with a null `counts` must never be pooled into a replace-rate comparison with a plan-sourced row.

root.description: Elements with an empty/absent `module_address` -- authored directly in the root module. Null for a changeset or template source, which has no module concept.

module.description: Elements with a non-empty `module_address` -- reached through a module call. `root + module == total` for a plan source; null for the other two. This split is the compression claim under test: the same resources moved from a different authoring surface.

counts.description: Each element bucketed on its `change.actions`, exactly one bucket per element, so the buckets sum to `total`: ["create"]->create, ["update"]->update, ["delete"]->delete, ["create","delete"] and ["delete","create"]->replace, ["no-op"]->no_op, ["read"]->read, anything else->other (and listed in `unclassified_actions`). Null for a `cloudformation-template` source, which has no actions.

replace.description: Destroyed and recreated rather than updated in place -- the count ROADMAP §2 names as the blast-radius headline.

other.description: An action pair the bucket mapping does not name (Terraform's `forget`, or a future action). Counted rather than dropped, and spelled out in `unclassified_actions`.

unclassified_actions.description: The verbatim `change.actions` value of every element that landed in the `other` bucket, present only when that count is non-zero. Makes an action Terraform adds later visible as unclassified instead of silently absorbed into a named bucket.

artifact.description: Path, relative to the trial dir, of the persisted artifact the counts were read from (e.g. "artifacts/plan.json", "steps/02-change-request/artifacts/ScenarioStack.template.json").

blast_radius_unavailable.description: Why `blast_radius` is absent on this row -- present only when it is, and never alongside it. A trial run before the verifier persisted its plan/template into /logs/artifacts reads "no artifacts/ ..." or "no plan.json or *.template.json under artifacts/": the field is not recoverable after the fact from anything else the trial kept, so the row carries the reason instead of a fabricated zero.

rbw.description: OPTIONAL profile column, READ-BEFORE-WRITE: output tokens emitted before the first mutation of the arm's own entry file (`lib/scenario-stack.ts` / `main.ts` / `main.tf`), counting Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit on that file and Bash redirects into it. The comprehension-cost proxy ROADMAP §3 finding 1 rests on. Emitted by gates/emit_result.py from metrics/extract_signals.py::trial_signals at gate time, not extracted post-hoc from a job dir that may be gone. ABSENT when the trial left no session transcript to scan (agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl); `tokens` is null WITHIN the object when a transcript exists but the entry file was never mutated -- the two cases are different and are not collapsed. Multi-step: rbw is a share, so it is never summed across steps -- the top-level numbers are the FINAL step's and `steps` carries each step's own.

tokens.description: Output tokens before the first entry-file mutation. Null when the entry file was never mutated in this trial (or step).

msgs.description: Assistant messages before that first mutation, deduplicated by `message.id` (a session jsonl repeats `usage` on every content block, so a naive sum double-counts -- docs/signal-extraction.md §1).

output_tokens.description: The denominator: total output tokens in the scanned session.

pct.description: 100 * tokens / output_tokens -- the comparable figure; the absolute scales with trial size. Null whenever `tokens` is.

steps.description: Per-step breakdown, present only on a multi-step trial: step output-dir name -> the same four fields for that step alone.

escape_hatch.description: OPTIONAL profile column: did the solution ever leave the arm's L2 abstraction? An EVER-USED flag scanned across every write to the entry file, not a final-state check. awscdk: `Cfn*`, addPropertyOverride, addOverride, defaultChild, escapeHatch. terraconstructs: a provider/aws import or a raw `new Aws*`/`new DataAws*`. hcl-modules: a `resource "aws_*"` block beside the module calls. "n/a" for hcl-raw, which is provider resources by construction and has no abstraction to leave -- distinct from "no", and never pooled with it. Multi-step: "yes" if any step escaped. ABSENT when the trial left no session transcript to scan (patterns in metrics/extract_signals.py::ESCAPE).
